Root cause: `collate_meta_tensor` only handled `MetaObj` and `Mapping` batch elements, so when `ImageDataset` (with `image_only=False`) returns per-sample `(image, meta, label)` tuples, it fell back to `default_collate`, which stacks the `MetaTensor`s without collating their meta dicts — leaving raw reader metadata (including 0-d numpy arrays from the Nifti header) attached to the batch tensor. `decollate_batch` then tried to iterate those 0-d arrays and crashed. The fix (1) makes `collate_meta_tensor` recurse into tuple/list batch elements so each field (image, meta, label) is collated via the MetaObj path, and (2) hardens `decollate_batch`/`_non_zipping_check` to treat 0-d numpy arrays as non-iterable scalars (as was already done for 0-d tensors), covering batches produced by a plain `default_collate` DataLoader. Verified with ImageDataset+MetaTensor reproductions (both collate paths) and the existing decollate/collate/image_dataset/meta_tensor test suites all pass.
